title: Dita Von Teese
description: American vedette, burlesque dancer, model, and businesswoman
wiki_lead:
Heather Renée Sweet (born September 28, 1972), known professionally as Dita Von Teese, is an American vedette, burlesque dancer, model, actress, and businesswoman. She is credited with re-popularizing burlesque performance, earning the moniker "Queen of Burlesque".
Von Teese has appeared in CSI: Crime Scene Investigation, RuPaul's Drag Race, The Masked Dancer, The Curious Creations of Christine McConnell, among other television productions. She is also known for her short marriage to singer Marilyn Manson as well as performing in his music videos. Von Teese has released two books on burlesque history, fetishism and beauty. She has toured the world with her burlesque shows in cities like London, Berlin, New York and Paris. Among her special guests on the tours are Dirty Martini, Perle Noire, Ginger Valentine, Jett Adore and Playboy model Gia Genevieve. Von Teese has been a special guest at the Parisian venue Crazy Horse several times. From 2007 to 2013, she was a global ambassador for Cointreau and in 2010–2011 she was the face of Perrier. She has also created four perfumes under the brand Dita Von Teese Perfumes. She also has her own brand of lingerie, as well as stockings under the name Secrets in Lace and luxurious cardigans for Australian online store Wheels & Dollbaby.

Early life
Von Teese was born Heather Renée Sweet in Rochester, Michigan, the second of three daughters. When she was five, her family moved to West Branch, Michigan. Describing her hometown, she says, "It's a universe away from the colored Klieg lights of Hollywood and Paris. But on weekend afternoons, my mom and I had a front seat on a rocket ship to those faraway worlds by way of the old movies starring the most glamorous creatures – Betty Grable, Mae West, Carmen Miranda, Marlene Dietrich... They were our muses." Her father was a machinist and her mother a manicurist. She is of English, Scottish, Armenian, and German heritage. Von Teese has stated that one of her grandmothers was half-Armenian and was adopted. Von Teese is known for her fascination with 1940s cinema and classic vintage style. This began at a young age and was fostered by her mother, who would buy clothes for her daughter to dress up. Her mother was a fan of old, Golden Age-era Hollywood films, and from her, Von Teese developed a fascination with the actresses of that day, especially Betty Grable.
She was classically trained as a ballet dancer from an early age, and danced solo at age 13 for a local ballet company. Though she originally wanted to be a ballerina, Von Teese states that "by 15, I was as good as I'd ever be." She was later to incorporate this element into her burlesque shows, where she frequently goes en pointe. The family relocated from Michigan to Orange County, California, when her father's job moved. Von Teese attended University High School in Irvine, California.

grok_lead: Dita Von Teese (born Heather RenÃ©e Sweet; September 28, 1972) is an American vedette, burlesque dancer, model, businesswoman, and author renowned as the "Queen of Burlesque" for her pivotal role in revitalizing the art form through elaborate, glamorous performances that blend vintage aesthetics with contemporary empowerment. Born in Rochester, Michigan, and raised in a small farming town before moving to Orange County, California, at age 13, she developed an early fascination with 1930s and 1940s cinema icons like Betty Grable and Rita Hayworth, which shaped her signature pin-up style. Her career began in the 1990s as a pin-up model and go-go dancer, influenced by the Los Angeles rave scene, drag culture, and a job at a lingerie store that ignited her interest in stylized eroticism and fashion. By 2002, she adopted her stage nameâoriginally a misspelling of "Von Treese"âfollowing her Playboy cover appearance, marking her transition to burlesque stardom. Von Teese's burlesque career exploded in the early 2000s, with her debut professional performance in 1992 evolving into sold-out international tours and residencies, including a signature martini glass routine that has become iconic and even inspired elements in Taylor Swift's 2022 "Bejeweled" music video. She has headlined major venues such as the London Palladium, Folies BergÃ¨re in Paris, and The Venetian in Las Vegas, where she maintains ongoing residencies, and launched four full-length revues like Glamonatrix (2017â2023) and the narrative-driven Diamonds and Dust (2025âpresent). Credited with transforming burlesque from a male-gaze spectacle into a female-centric art emphasizing technical precision, elaborate costumes, and escapist fantasy, she has collaborated with designers like Jean-Paul Gaultier and Jenny Packham to create opulent sets and attire. Her media presence extends to acting roles in films such as Don't Worry Darling (2022) and television appearances on shows like CSI and Queer Eye, alongside music videos for artists including Green Day. As an entrepreneur, Von Teese launched her eponymous lingerie line in 2010, followed by Von Follies collections, signature perfumes, and a French gin brand, while her authorship includes the New York Times bestseller Your Beauty Mark: The Ultimate Guide to Eccentric Beauty (2015) and the forthcoming Fashioning the Femme Totale (2026). She has received accolades such as the amfAR Award of Courage (2008) and served as MAC Viva Glam spokesperson (2006â2008), using her platform to advocate for LGBTQ+ rights, cancer research, and feminist causes against ageism and beauty standards. In her personal life, she was married to musician Marilyn Manson from December 2005 to January 2007, citing irreconcilable differences including infidelity and substance abuse as reasons for the split; the pair had been together for nearly five years prior. At 53, Von Teese continues to redefine glamour through her 30-year career, emphasizing self-expression and longevity in performance.
